messages:
Maya Ortiz: hi all — just got a support ticket, customer reports huge p95/p99 latency spikes hitting them ~09:10 UTC. I see the same on global dashboards, p99 from 220ms -> 1.8s. queue_length metric spiked.
Kevin Li: yikes. which route/model? any correlation with model changes?
Maya Ortiz: most traffic is to text-gen-v2 with default concurrency. A small subset of keys are getting most of the backlog. grouping by api_key shows a client with a sudden burst of long-context requests.
Alice (oncall): putting it in #incident for visibility. @Kevin can you pull the worker queue backlog? `redwoodctl metrics tail --name=serve/queue_length --window=30m`
Kevin Li: running it now. result: queue_length on pool "gen-v2-gpu-a" jumped to ~420 at 09:12, normally <30. p99 CPU on workers also jumped to 96%.
Ben R.: that sounds like worker saturation -> admission control kicking in and causing head-of-line delays. any signs of stuck requests (lots of retries)?
Maya Ortiz: logs show many long-token generations from that client, average tokens ~1500. KV cache misses are high for those requests (cache hit 22%). could be they changed prompt sizing.
Alice (oncall): immediate mitigations we can do now:
- apply per-key rate limit for offending api_key (support ticket id: #23456)
- lower route concurrency for text-gen-v2 from 16 -> 8
- enable fallback to cpu-quantized variant for bursty requests
Who can patch admission control quickly?
Kevin Li: I can push a temp policy. Patch:
```
admission_control:
  route: "/v1/text"
  max_concurrency: 8
  per_api_key:
    "ak_live_XXXX": 20r/s
```
Deploying in 2m.
Maya Ortiz: also turning on prefix KV caching for that pool (aggressive TTL) to try and reduce recompute for repeated prompts.
sre-bot: detected config change: admission_control updated by Kevin Li at 09:18 UTC — starting rollout to pool gen-v2-gpu-a
deploy-bot: canary started for admission-control (canary=2 nodes)
Ben R.: is there any chance routing misconfiguration sent more traffic to this pool? routing logs show a recent spike in requests tagged `region:eu` routed to this pool instead of eu-west pool.
Kevin Li: good catch — found a job that cleaned a routing tag yesterday (infra:cleanup-job). it removed a sticky region preference for some customers. rolling back that change now.
Maya Ortiz: after lowering concurrency + per-key rate limit, queue length dropped to ~45 within 4 minutes, p99 down to 480ms. still above baseline.
Alice (oncall): next steps (owner assignments):
- Kevin: follow up with infra to revert sticky-routing cleanup and run a canary validation job. (owner)
- Ben: dig into worker hotspots, gather flamegraphs for 09:10-09:25 window. (owner)
- Maya: coordinate with support to notify customer of temporary rate limit and mitigation steps, include repro steps and ask for sample request ids.
- SRE: prepare autoscale warmup for dedicated pool if we need to add capacity instantly.
Ben R.: initial flamegraph points to a handful of functions in tokenizer and attention kernel where latency is concentrated. looks like long sequences + repeated attention matrix allocations. possible memory churn.
Kevin Li: created infra rollback PR and started a hotfix deploy for routing. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/PR-987
Maya Ortiz: customer sent sample request ids. repro locally with `redwood-local run --model text-gen-v2 --req-file sample-ids.txt --concurrency 5`. I can reproduce 1.6s p99 locally when KV cache disabled.
Ben R.: that confirms KV cache pressure. plan: bump cache size for gen-v2 pool and change cache eviction policy to LRU+pin for repeated prompts.
Alice (oncall): if autoscale is needed, use the hot path: `infra scale-up pool gen-v2-gpu-a --nodes 8 --priority emergency` (SRE only).
Kevin Li: routing rollback finished and validated. traffic is now split correctly by region. queue_length stabilized ~22 and p99 290ms.
Maya Ortiz: summarizing timeline for support ticket:
- 09:10 UTC: sudden burst from one client -> queue backing up
- 09:12: queue_length -> 420, p99 -> 1.8s
- 09:18: admission-control policy applied + per-key rate limit
- 09:22: routing rollback
- 09:26: queue_norm ~22, p99 ~290ms
Ben R.: follow-ups: increase default KV cache quota for gen-v2 pool, add an alert for single-api_key request rate > 100r/s, add a dashboard tile showing per-api_key queue contribution.
Maya Ortiz: writing runbook note and will attach commands and logs. runbook snippet:
```
- check queues: redwoodctl metrics get serve/queue_length --pool {pool}
- identify hot api keys: redwoodctl logs query "api_key" --group-by api_key --window 30m --top 10
- emergency mitigate: redwoodctl adm update --max-concurrency 8 --per-key ak:XXXX:20r/s
```
Alice (oncall): thanks team. support notified customer of temporary throttling and offered to coordinate quota increase once they spread requests or move to Dedicated. closing slack thread after attaching runbook to ticket.
sre-bot: incident note saved to #incidents/1762509876 (summary: queueing/backpressure due to bursty long-context client; mitigations: admission-control and routing rollback)
Maya Ortiz: closing here, will follow up with a short postmortem and action items. :thumbsup:
